# routeur_provider_credential (Resource)

An upstream LLM provider API key held by the organisation: the key the gateway uses for that provider's traffic. An organisation holds at most one credential per provider. The key is verified against the provider before it is stored, sealed at rest and never returned; only its `fingerprint` is shown.

Set the key with exactly one of `key` (kept in state, marked sensitive) or `key_wo` + `key_wo_version` (write-only: never stored in the plan or state; needs Terraform 1.11 or later). If the key is changed outside Terraform, the changed `fingerprint` makes the next plan send the configured key again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Key kept in state (marked sensitive). Changing it rotates the credential
# in place.
resource "routeur_provider_credential" "openai" {
  provider_name = "openai"
  label         = "prod"
  key           = var.openai_api_key
}

# Write-only key (Terraform 1.11 or later): never stored in the plan or
# state. Bump key_wo_version to send a new key.
resource "routeur_provider_credential" "anthropic" {
  provider_name  = "anthropic"
  label          = "prod"
  key_wo         = var.anthropic_api_key
  key_wo_version = 1
}

variable "openai_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "anthropic_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) Label, 1–60 characters without leading or trailing whitespace, e.g. `prod`.
- `provider_name` (String) Upstream provider, e.g. `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, `deepseek` or `mistral`. Providers routeur.ai adds later work too: a value this provider version does not know is a warning, and the API decides. An organisation can hold one credential per provider. Set at create only; changing it replaces the credential. (The API calls this field `provider`, a name Terraform reserves.)

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the gateway uses the credential. Defaults to `true`; removing the argument enables it again.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The provider API key, 8–512 characters. Stored in state (sensitive). Changing it rotates the credential in place: the new key is verified, and the gateway switches to it without a gap. Conflicts with `key_wo`.
- `key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The provider API key, 8–512 characters, as a write-only argument: never stored in the plan or state (Terraform 1.11 or later). Terraform cannot see when it changes, so bump `key_wo_version` to send a new key. Requires `key_wo_version`; conflicts with `key`.
- `key_wo_version` (Number) Any number, changed to send `key_wo` again — rotating the credential in place when the key differs. Requires `key_wo`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `fingerprint` (String) Display form of the stored key, e.g. `sk-proj…a91f` (`…a91f` for short keys). Changes when the key is rotated; never reveals the key.
- `id` (String) Public id of the credential (`cred_…`).
- `updated_at` (String) When it was last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# id: the credential id. The key cannot be read back: the first apply
# after an import sends the configured key once (nothing changes if it is
# the stored key).
import {
  to = routeur_provider_credential.openai
  id = "cred_7"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By id. The key cannot be read back: the first apply after an import sends
# the configured key once (nothing changes if it is the stored key).
terraform import routeur_provider_credential.openai cred_7
```
